record.tranche_reason: Tests noisy-label learning behavior in multi-domain image translation, an extension of the claim to a different task and model setting.
record.gate_note: The paper's main experiments compare image-translation methods under synthetic and real-world label noise; they do not test fitting completely random labels, unstructured inputs, training time, or regularization claims. The training-trajectory result in Figure 10(i)(c) is the relevant result for V6. The memorization effect cited from Arpit et al. is prior work, not a result row.
record.test_reason: The study reports classifier test-accuracy trajectories under noisy-label training in image translation and explicitly interprets their early peaks and later declines as learning clean patterns before fitting noise. This bears indirectly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, RMIT usually improves generated-image classification accuracy over StarGAN but sometimes worsens FID; advanced variants improve that tradeoff. The authors also interpret early classifier test-accuracy peaks and subsequent declines as memorization and report mitigation through robust classifiers and virtual cycle consistency.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains multi-domain image-to-image translation GANs with label-noise-robust classification and cycle-consistency losses; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The trajectory result is shown for symmetric noise at μ = 0.5 with a naive classifier; the paper reports that label-noise-robust classifiers and virtual cycle consistency mitigate the memorization effect.
record.problems: The relevant trajectory is figure-only and is not numerically reported in the text. It concerns a classifier embedded in image translation under noisy labels, not standard networks trained on fully random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure a behavior named by V1–V6. Quantitative CA and FID comparisons measure image-translation performance, not the claim versions' random-label fitting behavior.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit together with test error approaching chance across corruption fractions. Generated-image classification accuracy is a different outcome.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Direct, separate learning trajectories for clean and corrupted training examples; comparison with fully random labels.

missing.what: The authors explicitly report that forward correction, co-teaching, and virtual cycle consistency mitigate the memorization-associated trajectory. Record this qualitative comparison separately; it does not establish that clean-before-noise learning disappears.

record.verdict_notes: No numerical curve values are available in the supplied text. Mitigation of test-accuracy decline alone does not warrant a limits_scope or challenges verdict on V6's learning-order claim.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption changes.
Training fit and test error across corruption rates for standard networks on the claim's task.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting or affect true-label generalization.

The study uses noisy rather than fully random labels and does not compare learning of real labels against fully random labels; the trajectory evidence is for the classifier in its image-translation setting.

rows.value: Figure only; authors state all models achieve their best test accuracy early in training, then scores decrease at the end.
rows.note: The text attributes the decline to memorization and says the DNN classifier first memorizes a simple pattern (clean labeled data), then fits noisy labeled data. The six model curves are not separately quantified in the supplied text.
rows.check: The reported trajectory and authors' interpretation are accurately recorded, but test accuracy does not directly separate fitting clean and corrupted training examples. The baseline is the earlier test-accuracy peak. Test accuracy was computed every 100 iterations; curves were smoothed. The six models are pooled in this row rather than recorded separately.
